accuracy.evidence: Blue whale up to about 30 m and the largest animal known to have lived (NOAA Fisheries 'Blue whale'); great white shark adults about 4–5 m (NOAA Fisheries / Florida Museum ichthyology); green sea turtle shell about 1 m (NOAA Fisheries); clownfish about 10 cm (Australian Museum / Smithsonian Ocean); seahorses are bony fish with gills, fins and a swim bladder (Smithsonian Ocean 'Seahorses', Project Seahorse); sea stars are echinoderms, not fish, moving on tube feet; jellyfish have no bones or brain (NOAA Ocean Service 'Are starfish fish?', 'Do jellyfish have brains?'); octopuses jet by expelling water through a siphon; crabs walk on legs, often sideways; whales are mammals (Natural History Museum). Kid comparisons (hand, as long as you are tall, a car, longer than two buses) match these lengths.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented child ideas about sea life: everything in the sea is a fish (shape prediction, fish sort, m1, tags all and star), a seahorse is not a fish because of its name and shape (fish prediction, p2, tag horse), the biggest animal ever was a dinosaur or a shark (size prediction, p1, tag dino), whales are fish (m6, whale card feedback), and counting animals instead of kinds when judging variety (reef prediction 4 vs 2 kinds, m5, tag count).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagovar is built on variety itself: a size line that only accepts the next-smallest animal and then labels each with a real-world length, five drawn body-shape silhouettes (star, rope, pancake, spiky ball, eight arms) to match, a fish / not-a-fish sort whose feedback names each animal's body plan, movement lanes that animate the animal across once matched, and a reef where tapping counts kinds rather than animals. flagocean (what the ocean is), flagseaneed (needs) and flagwhale (whale vs fish traits) share none of these; the distinct gate passed under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea is discovered by doing: dropping the shark first is refused because the clownfish is smaller; the sea star card refused by the spiky box is told its real shape; putting the seahorse in 'Not a fish' triggers 'Surprise! A seahorse is a fish...'; tapping a second clownfish on the reef is told the count of kinds stays the same; the reef ends at 9 animals but 6 kinds.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with a tempting wrong option, each disproved by the task that follows: 'a dinosaur' for the biggest animal ever (the size line ends with the blue whale), 'yes, they all look like fish' (five non-fish shapes), 'no, it is a kind of horse' for the seahorse (it sorts as a fish), and '4 kinds' for 3 clownfish and 1 crab (the reef tally counts kinds).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions (biggest animal, seahorse, sea star, octopus movement, counting kinds, hand-sized animal, are all sea animals fish-shaped). Wrong options carry tags dino, horse, star, all, move, count and size, each with its own message naming the slip, e.g. 'Count kinds, not animals: crabs are one kind and the turtle is another, so 2 kinds.'

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes the kid and adult readability limits. Kid sentences are short and concrete ('An eel is long and thin.'), with fish defined by gills and fins before it is used. Number items stay within KS1: adding two small groups, counting in 2s and 5s. Young-mode buttons are 56 px tall with larger text.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs cover size, shape, fish vs not fish and movement, one idea each. Adult: curriculum link and key words, sizes with numbers and the classification of each animal, four named mistakes, then what the lab does. No filler pattern matched; the 12% duplicate gate passed against 563 What Is the Ocean?, 643 What Ocean Animals Need and 555 Whales & Dolphins Are Mammals.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android light and dark and iPhone 13 light after Show me on every step. Fixed from the first pass: the octopus silhouette read as a lollipop, now a larger head with eight thick, spread arms; size-slot names were squeezed 12 px 'great white shark', now one word at 13 px with the full comparisons listed above the line once ordered; the moving names stay inside their lanes. Real pointer drags (size cards, shape card) and reef taps were tested at 390 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin: one per remaining animal on the size line, one per shape, Fish / Not a fish, one per way of moving, and one per reef animal with an aria-label naming it. The canvas aria-label and live region carry every message, including the kinds tally. walk.cjs passed axe WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console or page errors.
